items.t: Ukraine’s fiber-optic drones get squeezed by AI data center demand
items.d: Ukraine competes with Russia and data centers for China’s optical fiber supply.
items.x:
Impervious to battlefield jamming, drones physically connected to human operators by miles of fiber-optic cables have become such a common weapon of war in Ukraine that trees and fields are strewn with tangled cables thinner than fishing lines. But importing such fiber-optic material from China has become more costly as drone warfare’s needs compete with global demand from AI data centers for the same limited supply—and so Ukrainian drone makers have been adapting.
Since the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022, the Ukrainians have been forced out of necessity to continually develop battlefield innovations involving first-person view (FPV) quadcopter drones and other heavier types of drones. But it was the Russian military that first deployed unjammable fiber-optic drones to repel Ukrainian forces’ cross-border incursion into the Kursk Oblast in 2024.

items.t: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
items.d: AlphaProof Code agents wrote three million lines of proofs in Lean to verify Signal’s core encryption.
items.x:
AlphaProof Code agents wrote over three million lines of machine-checked proof in Lean to verify the core cryptographic protections in Signal down to machine instructions.
How Google DeepMind researchers built a new agentic framework that formally verified the code of Signal’s cryptographic protocol — long considered to be a grand security challenge
Today, we’re sharing a milestone in software security long considered to be a grand security challenge: Google DeepMind researchers guided AI agents to mathematically prove key security properties of the actual code underlying the Signal protocol, the technology that protects billions of private conversations in apps like Signal and Google Messages.
This breakthrough discovery was made using AlphaProof Code, a novel agentic framework for formal verification at unprecedented depth that combines human expertise with AI agents. Formal verification—mathematically proving code runs correctly without flaws—is the highest standard of security assurance; however, it is difficult and often labor-intensive.
Our work marks the first time AI has been used to formally verify a widely deployed cryptographic protocol at this depth.

items.t: Adaspace Put AI on Satellites. Now It Wants to Sell Computing Time.
items.d: Editor’s note: This article is republished from Jumpstart, a TechNode Group publication. At an algorithms competition in Guangzhou, a team working on traffic analysis sent its model somewhere unusual: to a satellite already in orbit…
items.x:
Editor’s note: This article is republished from Jumpstart , a TechNode Group publication.
At an algorithms competition in Guangzhou, a team working on traffic analysis sent its model somewhere unusual: to a satellite already in orbit. Jiazhihuihang, part of Chinese transport technology company PCI Technology, worked with Adaspace to run the model in space. The satellite could process imagery before sending the analysis back to Earth. If the job is to extract information about a road network, there is less reason to transmit every pixel before getting started.
For Adaspace, the experiment pointed to a different kind of business. A company that builds satellites for customers could also give them somewhere to run their software. The Chengdu company expects its shares to begin trading in Hong Kong on November 13. Its IPO will help fund the engineering needed to take that idea beyond individual demonstrations.
Adaspace began in 2018 with a smaller engineering problem: how to make AI work aboard a satellite in the first place. Its early work centred on payloads, the equipment a satellite carries to perform its mission. In December that year, it launched its first AI application satellite.
The early satellites used onboard computing to help with their own work.

items.t: Otter AI can now follow conversations across 30+ languages
items.d: Otter AI just added support for 27 languages and revealed an upcoming feature that can follow along if speakers switch between languages.
items.x:
Otter AI just added support for 27 languages and revealed an upcoming feature that can follow along if speakers switch between languages.
Otter.ai, the AI-powered note-taking tool, announced Tuesday that it’s expanding its multilingual capabilities, including a new multilingual transcription feature that can follow conversations as speakers switch between languages during the same meeting.
The company is also adding support for 27 languages, its largest language expansion to date. Once the rollout is complete, Otter will support 31 languages in total, making the platform more accessible to international teams.
The upcoming feature will automatically detect language changes and continue transcribing without requiring users to adjust settings. For example, a call could move from English to Korean to Portuguese, with Otter following the conversation throughout.
The update aims to address a common challenge for global teams, where language differences can make meetings and collaboration more difficult.
“Otter is breaking down language barriers so any company, no matter where they’re based, can build a system of record for the decisions for voice AI communication,” an Otter spokesperson told TechCrunch.
Thirteen of the new languages are available now: Mandarin Chinese, Korean…

items.t: أستراليا تتجه لتشديد رقابة الذكاء الاصطناعي بعد حادثة OpenAI
items.d: أعلنت أستراليا خطة لفرض ضوابط أمن وسلامة إلزامية على شركات الذكاء الاصطناعي المتقدم، بعد مراجعة حادثة وصول غير مصرح به نفذها وكيل من OpenAI إلى بوابة حكومية.
items.x:
تعتزم أستراليا فرض التزامات أمن وسلامة إلزامية على مطوري الذكاء الاصطناعي المتقدم، بعد حادثة وصول غير مصرح به لوكيل من OpenAI إلى نظام حكومي.
أعلنت الحكومة الأسترالية عزمها إدراج متطلبات إلزامية للسلامة والأمن في تشريعات معايير الذكاء الاصطناعي، تستهدف الشركات المطورة للنماذج الأكثر تقدمًا التي ترغب في العمل داخل البلاد، وذلك في أعقاب مراجعة حادثة وصول غير مصرح به نفذها وكيل ذكاء اصطناعي تابع لشركة OpenAI إلى نظام حكومي أسترالي.
وبحسب الإعلان الحكومي الرسمي، تتضمن الخطة إنشاء جهة رقابية متخصصة مقترحة لمتابعة التزام الشركات بمتطلبات السلامة، مع إمكانية فرض عقوبات كبيرة على المخالفين بعد إقرار الإطار التشريعي. ولم تدخل هذه الالتزامات حيز التنفيذ بعد، إذ ما زالت الحكومة تعمل على تفاصيل القانون والتشاور بشأنه.
تريد الحكومة إلزام الشركات المعنية بالحفاظ على ضوابط أمنية خلال تطوير النماذج ونشرها، وتحديد المخاطر الجسيمة وإدارتها، والسماح بتقييم مستقل للنماذج، والإبلاغ السريع عن الحوادث إلى السلطات الأسترالية. وتشمل الالتزامات أيضًا نشر أطر السلامة والأمن الخاصة بالشركات، والامتثال للمعايير والقواعد التي قد تتغير مع تطور التكنولوجيا.
وتقترح الحكومة أن تعمل الجهة الرقابية الجديدة بالتعاون مع المعهد الأسترالي لسلامة الذكاء الاصطناعي لتوفير الخبرة التقنية والإشراف.

items.t: ترامب: FBI ينظر في قضية مزاعم التجسس المرتبطة برئيس إنفيديا
items.d: قال ترامب إن FBI ينظر في قضية مزاعم التجسس التي تناولتها تقارير بشأن رئيس إنفيديا جنسن هوانغ، من دون توضيح نطاق الإجراءات أو تأكيد توجيه اتهامات.
items.x:
قال ترامب إن مكتب FBI ينظر في قضية مزاعم التجسس المتعلقة برئيس إنفيديا جنسن هوانغ، دون توضيح نطاق التحقيق أو تأكيد أي اتهامات رسمية.
قال الرئيس الأمريكي دونالد ترامب إن مكتب التحقيقات الفيدرالي الأمريكي (FBI) ينظر في قضية أثارتها تقارير صحفية بشأن علاقة الرئيس التنفيذي لشركة إنفيديا (Nvidia)، جنسن هوانغ، بسيدة أعمال نسبت إليها مصادر استخباراتية أمريكية صلات محتملة بالصين. ولم يوضح ترامب نطاق نظر المكتب في القضية أو ما إذا كان قد فُتح تحقيق رسمي يستهدف هوانغ شخصيًا.
وجاءت تصريحات ترامب خلال حديثه إلى الصحفيين في البيت الأبيض يوم 9 نوفمبر 2026، وفقًا لتغطية وكالة رويترز. وقال الرئيس الأمريكي إنه تحدث إلى هوانغ بشأن التقارير، وإن رئيس إنفيديا أبلغه بأنه لم يكن يعلم بالمزاعم المتعلقة بسيدة الأعمال المذكورة. ولا يمثل هذا التصريح إثباتًا لصحة تلك المزاعم.
أشار ترامب إلى أن مكتب التحقيقات الفيدرالي ينظر في الأمر، من دون تقديم تفاصيل عن الإجراءات المتخذة أو تحديد الأشخاص الذين قد يشملهم أي تحقيق. ولم يتوافر تأكيد مستقل صادر عن المكتب يوضح طبيعة القضية أو نطاقها، ولذلك لا يمكن الجزم بأن هوانغ يخضع لتحقيق جنائي أو أن السلطات توصلت إلى أدلة تثبت وقوع تجسس.
سبق أن أعلن مجلس إدارة إنفيديا تشكيل مسار للتحقيق المستقل في التقارير التي تتناول استهداف رئيسها التنفيذي بعملية استخباراتية مزعومة، بإشراف مديرين مستقلين وبمساعدة مستشارين قانونيين خارجيين.

items.t: Alibaba's Qianwen Office 2.0 Brings AI Agents Into Team Workspaces and Event-Triggered Tasks
items.d: Qianwen Office 2.0 adds shared agent workspaces linked to DingTalk chats and docs, event-triggered Automatic Tasks, in-place co-editing and a mobile app.
items.x:
According to DingTalk, Alibaba's workplace-software platform, Qianwen Office 2.0 launched on November 9 as a "Team Agent" for individuals and organizations rather than a single-user assistant. The company says all features are now available in the Qianwen Office client and calls it the product's biggest upgrade since launch about three months ago.
The headline feature is "Collaboration," which DingTalk describes as the first to support several people and an agent working together. A team creates a shared space for a project and gets a dedicated "digital employee." The space can link DingTalk group chats, documents, AI spreadsheets and AI meeting notes, run several conversations in parallel, and let members assign tasks that the digital employee turns into progress summaries and follow-up to-dos. Product documentation notes that an ordinary group member needs a group administrator's approval before a chat can be linked.
A "human-AI co-creation" mode lets users open DingTalk documents, AI spreadsheets or Yida low-code apps inside a task conversation, select paragraphs, cells or slides, mark several comments and submit them at once so the AI edits the original in place. DingTalk says several people and agents can co-edit at the same time.

items.x:
The AI company is expected to set its valuation range this week, the Wall Street Journal reported.
Launching a major tech IPO would seem risky right now, shortly after one of Nasdaq’s biggest selloffs and amid revelations that a CEO central to the AI boom had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But that isn’t deterring Anthropic, which is moving ahead with its listing plans, according to The Wall Street Journal.
Anthropic plans to set a valuation range this week and begin trading on Thursday or Friday of next week, the Journal reported.
Investors will look to Anthropic’s valuation to gauge the strength of the AI boom. Some institutional investors are now pushing for a valuation below the $1.5 trillion target discussed as recently as last week, a figure that was itself considerably below the $2 trillion floated a few months ago, the report said.
OpenAI, Anthropic’s main rival, was reportedly valued at $1.25 trillion last week after the ChatGPT maker raised $11 billion in fresh capital, short of the $20 billion it had initially sought.

items.t: Everything we know so far about the Nvidia spy scandal targeting CEO Jensen Huang
items.d: The leather-jacketed CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, has acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, spurring an investigation by his company and intense discussions worldwide. Recent reporting noted that since last year, US…
items.x:
The leather-jacketed CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, has acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, spurring an investigation by his company and intense discussions worldwide. Recent reporting noted that since last year, US intelligence reports had identified Alice Huang (no relation) as not only the exec for an AI compute company renting access to Nvidia GPUs, but also a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security.
In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies, including the “neoclouds” like Coreweave who have been some of its biggest customers. So far, Nvidia and Jensen Huang have said that they have “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised,” but that hasn’t settled things as the investigation continues.

items.d: The PR firm was enlisted shortly after an October 2025 New York Times report described Alice Huang's business dealings with Jensen Huang, Wired reported.
items.x:
The PR firm was enlisted shortly after an October 2025 New York Times report described Alice Huang's business dealings with Jensen Huang, Wired reported.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang hired Heller Inc., a crisis communications firm known for handling sex scandals, at least a year before he publicly acknowledged an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of spying for China, Wired reported.
Heller Inc. founder Risa Heller has advised prominent men through personal scandals and sexual misconduct accusations, according to a 2023 New York Magazine profile. Her reported clients include former congressman Anthony Weiner, celebrity chef Mario Batali, and former New Yorker writer Jeffrey Toobin.
Wired also reported that Nvidia’s internal communications team was told to copy Heller Inc. on press inquiries about Huang shortly after an October 2025 New York Times report about whether Nvidia was helping Chinese companies evade U.S. chip export restrictions.
The Times reported that Megaspeed, a then little-known Singapore-based data center company with ties to China, had acquired nearly $2 billion worth of Nvidia chips.

items.x:
Six months before Nvidia's spy scandal erupted, Culper Research was already questioning Jensen Huang's unusually close relationship with a Chinese executive.
Six months before the Nvidia spy scandal emerged, the New York-based short seller firm Culper Research had already raised questions about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s unusually close relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that buys Nvidia chips. She is now suspected to be a Chinese spy.
The Nvidia CEO admitted to an extramarital affair over the weekend, and the company has now opened a formal investigation into his relationship with Alice Huang (who shares his last name but is not related). U.S. intelligence officials believe she was recruited by the Chinese government to collect intelligence on Jensen Huang and influence his position regarding U.S. export controls on advanced AI chips.
Culper’s May 13 report is resurfacing because it picked up on the connection between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang while investigating Megaspeed’s ties to Nvidia.

items.t: The race is on to sue Nvidia
items.d: Nvidia’s stock slid more than 4% after its board opened an investigation into Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and one securities law expert says the company’s earlier insistence that it was all “normal” could turn…
items.x:
Nvidia’s stock slid more than 4% after its board opened an investigation into Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and one securities law expert says the company’s earlier insistence that it was all “normal” could turn into a very expensive problem.
Nvidia’s stock slid more than 4% on Monday, the first trading day after its board said it would investigate CEO Jensen Huang over his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive U.S. intelligence believes was spying for China.
Securities lawyers were already moving. Schall, Brown & Schwartz, a Los Angeles shareholder-rights firm, was among the first to plant a flag, announcing Monday morning that it’s investigating whether Nvidia made false or misleading statements, or failed to disclose information pertinent to investors. Robert Bartlett, a Stanford Law professor and securities law expert, expects it to have plenty of company.
“I would definitely wager that there’ll be a filing,” Bartlett said in an interview Monday morning, adding that he wouldn’t be surprised if a case had been filed by the end of day. Plaintiffs’ lawyers have good reasons to be first in line; under federal securities law, the first complaint triggers a public notice, and investors then have 60 days to ask the court to be named lead plaintiff.

items.t: ميتا توسّع عالمياً تقنية الذكاء الاصطناعي للكشف عن حسابات المراهقين
items.d: أعلنت ميتا توسيع استخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي لتحديد حسابات المراهقين الذين يقدمون أعماراً غير دقيقة وإخضاعها لإجراءات الحماية، مع خطط لتوسيع التقنية على فيسبوك وThreads.
items.x:
ميتا توسع تقنية الذكاء الاصطناعي لاكتشاف حسابات المراهقين ذات الأعمار غير الدقيقة وتطبيق إجراءات الحماية، مع خطط للتوسع على فيسبوك وThreads.
أعلنت شركة ميتا توسيع نطاق استخدام تقنياتها القائمة على الذكاء الاصطناعي حول العالم، بهدف تحديد الحسابات التي يُعتقد أنها تعود إلى مراهقين أدخلوا أعماراً غير دقيقة عند التسجيل، وإخضاعها تلقائياً لتدابير الحماية المخصصة لهذه الفئة العمرية، وفقاً لبيان صحافي تلقت البوابة التقنية نسخته منه.
وتستخدم الشركة هذه التقنيات لرصد الحسابات التي يُحتمل أن يملكها مراهقون حتى عندما يشير تاريخ الميلاد المسجل إلى أن صاحب الحساب بالغ، وذلك لتطبيق إجراءات حماية تتناسب مع العمر الفعلي.

items.d: كشفت سنوفليك عن Business Ontology وCortex AI Gateway وقدرات جديدة في CoCo وCoWork، لتعزيز فهم وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي لبيانات المؤسسات وحوكمتهم وتنفيذ مهامهم.
items.x:
سنوفليك تكشف Business Ontology وCortex AI Gateway وقدرات جديدة في CoCo وCoWork لفهم بيانات المؤسسات وحوكمة وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي.
أعلنت شركة سنوفليك مجموعة من الأدوات والقدرات الجديدة المصممة لمساعدة المؤسسات في تشغيل وكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي بالاعتماد على سياق أعمال موحد وضوابط للحوكمة والأمن وإدارة التكاليف، وفقاً لبيان صحافي تلقت البوابة التقنية نسخته منه.
وشملت الإعلانات، التي قدمتها الشركة خلال مؤتمر «سنوفليك إكسبيديشن 2026»، ميزة Business Ontology وبوابة Cortex AI Gateway وقدرات جديدة في الوكيلين Snowflake CoCo وSnowflake CoWork.
تندرج ميزة Business Ontology ضمن قدرات Horizon Context في Snowflake Horizon Catalog، وتسمح للمؤسسات بتعريف مفاهيم الأعمال الأساسية بصورة موحدة، مثل «صافي الإيرادات»، وتحديد المسؤول عن كل تعريف وربطه بالبيانات ذات الصلة.
وتعمل الميزة مع Semantic Views وCortex Sense لتوفير سياق مشترك يمكن لوكلاء الذكاء الاصطناعي والتطبيقات والموظفين استخدامه، بحسب ما أوضحته الشركة.
أما بوابة Cortex AI Gateway فتستهدف توحيد الضوابط المطبقة على النماذج والأدوات والعمليات التي يستخدمها الوكلاء، بما يشمل الأمن والحوكمة وإدارة التكاليف، بدلاً من إدارة الاتصالات والضوابط بصورة منفصلة.
وقالت سنوفليك إن الوكلاء يتصلون بالنماذج وخوادم بروتوكول سياق النماذج (MCP) وأنظمة المؤسسات، ما يبرز الحاجة إلى إدارة موحدة لهذا الاستخدام.

items.t: «لِف» يعلن دمج العملة المستقرة USDU في تطبيقه المصرفي بالإمارات
items.d: أعلن لِف التابع لبنك الإمارات دبي الوطني تعاوناً مع يونيفرسال وأكوا ناو لدمج العملة المستقرة USDU، المسجلة لدى المصرف المركزي الإماراتي، ضمن منظومة خدماته الرقمية.
items.x:
لِف من بنك الإمارات دبي الوطني يتعاون مع يونيفرسال وأكوا ناو لدمج العملة المستقرة USDU المسجلة لدى المصرف المركزي ضمن خدماته المصرفية الرقمية.
أعلن «لِف» التابع لبنك الإمارات دبي الوطني تعاونه مع «يونيفرسال ديجيتال إنترناشونال» و«أكوا ناو الشرق الأوسط» لدمج العملة المستقرة USDU المدعومة بالدولار الأمريكي ضمن منظومته للخدمات المصرفية الرقمية، وفقاً لبيان صحافي تلقت البوابة التقنية نسخته منه.
وأوضح البيان أن USDU عملة مستقرة مسجلة لدى مصرف الإمارات العربية المتحدة المركزي بموجب نظام خدمات رمز الدفع، وأن «يونيفرسال» تتولى إصدارها، فيما تتولى «أكوا ناو» توفير البنية التحتية للأصول الرقمية وتوزيع العملة وتداول العملات الرقمية عبر تطبيق Liv X.
تأتي الخطوة بعد إطلاق خدمات تداول العملات الرقمية عبر تطبيق Liv X في عام 2025، بهدف توسيع عروض الأصول الرقمية وإتاحة إدارة الأنشطة المصرفية التقليدية ومحافظ الأصول الرقمية ضمن بيئة واحدة.
وبحسب البيان، ترتبط قيمة USDU بالدولار الأمريكي، وهي مدعومة باحتياطيات فعلية بالدولار بنسبة 1:1 محفوظة لدى بنوك إماراتية، مع التحقق منها عبر كشوفات شهرية متاحة للجمهور.

items.t: دراسة من F5: التشفير ما بعد الكمومي مستخدم في 56.7% من المواقع بالإمارات
items.d: كشف مسح أجرته مختبرات F5 أن 56.7% من المواقع الإلكترونية في الإمارات اعتمدت تقنيات التشفير ما بعد الكمومي، مقارنة بمتوسط عالمي بلغ 54%، مع تفاوت بين القطاعات.
items.x:
دراسة F5 ترصد اعتماد التشفير ما بعد الكمومي في 56.7% من المواقع الإلكترونية بالإمارات مقابل 54% عالمياً، مع تفاوت واضح بين القطاعات الحيوية.
أظهرت دراسة صادرة عن مختبرات شركة F5 أن 56.7% من المواقع الإلكترونية في دولة الإمارات اعتمدت تقنيات التشفير ما بعد الكمومي، مقارنة بمتوسط عالمي بلغ 54%، وفقاً لبيان صحافي تلقت البوابة التقنية نسخته منه.
واستند تقرير الشركة لعام 2026 إلى مسح لأكبر مليون موقع إلكتروني في العالم، إلى جانب تحليل تفصيلي للقطاعات والدول شمل أكبر 100 ألف نطاق إلكتروني، بهدف قياس الاستعداد للتشفير القادر على مواجهة التهديدات المستقبلية المرتبطة بالحوسبة الكمومية.
أظهر التحليل التفصيلي اعتماد تقنيات التشفير ما بعد الكمومي في 34.5% من المواقع بقطاع النفط والغاز، و35.2% في الاتصالات، و35.4% في القطاع الحكومي، و39.4% في قطاع المرافق والخدمات.
وفي المقابل، سجلت خدمات المستهلكين نسبة 58.8%، وقطاع التكنولوجيا 56.1%، والسلع الاستهلاكية 49.8%، بحسب الدراسة.
أشارت F5 إلى أن جزءاً مهماً من الارتفاع في مستوى الاعتماد يرتبط باستخدام منصات الحوسبة الطرفية وتوصيل المحتوى، ولا سيما Cloudflare التي فعّلت آليات تبادل مفاتيح هجينة مدعومة بالتشفير ما بعد الكمومي بصورة افتراضية.
وبحسب نتائج التقرير، تنخفض النسبة العالمية من 54% إلى 22% عند استبعاد النطاقات المستضافة على Cloudflare من مجموعة البيانات.

items.t: Jensen Huang pulls out of ElevenLabs Summit amid Nvidia controversy
items.d: The Nvidia CEO also pulled out of an Anthropic event earlier.
items.x:
The Nvidia CEO also pulled out of an Anthropic event earlier.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has pulled out of the ElevenLabs Summit scheduled for this Wednesday in New York, ElevenLabs, the voice AI company, confirmed Monday. He has also dropped out of other speaking engagements, including the Anthropic CEO Forum. Nvidia is an investor in ElevenLabs.
The withdrawals come after Huang admitted to an extramarital affair over the weekend, and Nvidia opened an investigation into his relationship with a possible Chinese spy.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” Huang said in a memo to the company.
The incident has rattled the AI industry, raising questions about Huang’s staying power as CEO and Nvidia’s own China ambitions.

items.t: The backlash about data centers might really just be about electricity
items.d: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known…
items.x:
As voters went to the polls across the US last week, I was in Ashburn, Virginia, part of what’s known as Data Center Alley—the world’s largest data center hub. It’s also where the backlash now sweeping the country arguably first began taking shape.
Driving through it is surreal. Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ.
It’s accepted wisdom in Big Tech that the war against data centers must be about something bigger than just data centers themselves. Two days after the midterms, OpenAI’s chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, wrote that data centers “have become a proxy for public unease about affordability, corporate power, and people losing control over their futures.” It’s a culture war, in other words.
But spending a few days in Data Center Alley left me wondering if it’s really the proxy that Lehane describes. I came away convinced that the data center backlash is more about electricity than Big Tech admits. The industry can improve its image, but it can’t escape the physical consequences of its enormous appetite for electricity.
Here’s why. There are two ways to power the sort of data center that AI companies want: connecting to the grid, or generating electricity onsite.

items.t: Anthropic releases new Mythos and Fable models amid RSI concerns
items.d: Anthropic says the new models "show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision," as well as in communicating more clearly with users.
items.x:
Anthropic says the new models "show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision," as well as in communicating more clearly with users.
Anthropic released new versions of its most advanced models on Monday, with the launch of Mythos 5.2 and Fable 5.2. The company says the new models “show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision,” and communicate more clearly with users.
Notably, Anthropic is lowering the cost of Fable from $10 to $8 per million input tokens. As a result, Fable 5.2 is now cheaper than its primary competitor GPT-6 Astra. Anthropic says that the new version of Fable will return responses 30% faster across effort levels. Faster inference serving is available for double the price.
Fable 5.2 is also compatible with zero data retention (ZDR) policies through the Enterprise Frontier Safeguards system, long a sticking point for many enterprise clients.
It’s Anthropic’s first model release since the arrival of a third-party report from the assessment group METR, which suggested the lab might be approaching recursive self-improvement (RSI) — or the ability for AI models to carry on model training independently.

items.t: Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy puts Nvidia’s China ambitions under scrutiny
items.d: Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy threatens to complicate Nvidia’s lobbying efforts to loosen U.S. chip export restrictions and maintain access to China’s lucrative AI market.
items.x:
Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy threatens to complicate Nvidia’s lobbying efforts to loosen U.S. chip export restrictions and maintain access to China’s lucrative AI market.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has never been quiet about his belief that the U.S. should continue selling AI chips to China, rather than shutting the country off from the technology. The revelation that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy threatens to complicate that argument.
The Financial Times reported Friday on the relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer. Jensen Huang admitted to the affair and apologized in a memo to the company on Sunday. U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was recruited by Chinese intelligence to gather information about the CEO and influence the company’s efforts to loosen chip export restrictions.
Nvidia’s independent directors, working with outside legal counsel, are investigating the matter, and Congress is already demanding answers.
The controversy comes at a sensitive moment for Nvidia. Historically, China has been a big market for the company. It has shrunk in recent years due to strict U.S. export controls and an aggressive push by Beijing for domestic alternatives.

items.t: Meta releases Muse Ember, a new lightweight model for agent execution
items.d: At 10 cents per million input tokens, Ember is significantly cheaper than frontier competitors like Haiku and Luna.
items.x:
At 10 cents per million input tokens, Ember is significantly cheaper than frontier competitors like Haiku and Luna.
Meta Superintelligence Lab released a new AI model on Monday called Muse Ember, the lab’s lightest and most cost-efficient AI model yet. In its release, Meta said Ember was “designed for complex reasoning execution and the work agents repeat all day: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction, and long document parsing.”
Meta particularly emphasized Ember’s cost-per-task, using Artificial Analysis’s composite benchmark score to show Ember as cheaper and smarter than competitors like Anthropic’s Haiku and OpenAI’s Luna.
Given the emphasis on low cost and accuracy at scale, Ember is designed to pair with a larger model like Meta’s Muse Wonder in an agentic harness. In the case of a customer-support agent, for instance, you might see a heavier model establishing rules for how to handle a particular issue, then sending a lighter-weight model to apply the rules across tens of thousands of cases. As Meta puts it in the announcement, “Muse Wonder plans, Muse Ember handles the volume.”
With volume-heavy use cases in mind, Meta also trained Ember to work well across different types of media, including text, images, and audio.

items.t: Claude Code is accidentally exposing secrets all over GitHub
items.d: "Do not ask again" prompt leads to passwords, API keys, and more being shared.
items.x:
Claude Code is leaking sensitive information on public GitHub instances thanks to a partial oversight in the way its settings files are handled. That's the finding of AI security researchers at Apiiro, who discovered thousands of secrets , including database passwords, API tokens, and root logins, amid Claude Code settings files embedded in GitHub repositories.
The leak stems from the way Claude Code handles user approval for automated shell commands. When a user chooses the "Yes, and don't ask again" option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local ".claude/settings.local.json" file on the user's computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it.
This isn't really a significant security issue if the settings file stays on the user's local machine (assuming that machine doesn't become compromised itself, of course). And Anthropic notes in its Claude Code documentation that this particular settings file gets added to the developer's global .gitignore list , which usually prevents it from being shared publicly.

items.t: Nancy Pelosi’s replacement is ready to regulate AI
items.d: As a California state senator, Scott Wiener authored legislation aimed at curbing the risks of advanced AI. Now, after winning a tight congressional race for former Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi’s open San Francisco seat, he could play…
items.x:
A new voice for AI regulation in Congress: Scott Wiener, who authored the country's first proposed frontier AI legislation, just won Nancy Pelosi's former congressional seat and is already pushing for federal action — warning that "we could sleepwalk into a disaster."
Recursive self-improvement is keeping him up at night: A recent report suggesting Anthropic may have achieved AI that meaningfully advances itself rattled Wiener, who sees it as proof that Congress is running out of time to act before losing control entirely.
He wants regulation with real teeth: Wiener is pushing for a powerful federal AI regulator, whistleblower protections, kill switches, and auditing requirements — and he's firmly against federal laws that would strip states of their own ability to regulate.
Cautious optimism, with caveats: Wiener is concerned about Congress's poor track record on tech regulation, wary of Trump's hostility to AI safety concerns, and hoping any crisis that forces action will be, as he puts it, "as small as possible."

items.t: جوجل تكشف عن نظامين جديدين لمعالجات TPU لتعزيز أمن الذكاء الاصطناعي وقدرات المعالجة
items.d: أعلنت جوجل نظامَي TPU 8tx وTPU 8i Max ضمن الجيل الثامن من معالجاتها المخصصة للذكاء الاصطناعي، مع التركيز على الحوسبة السرية ومضاعفة قدرات معالجة السياقات الطويلة.
items.x:
أعلنت جوجل نظامَي TPU 8tx وTPU 8i Max لتعزيز حماية بيانات الذكاء الاصطناعي وزيادة القدرة الحسابية وعرض نطاق الذاكرة لتطبيقات السياقات الطويلة.
أعلنت شركة جوجل توسيع الجيل الثامن من أنظمة وحدات معالجة الموتر (TPU) المخصصة للذكاء الاصطناعي، بإضافة نظامين جديدين هما TPU 8tx وTPU 8i Max، يستهدف الأول حماية البيانات والنماذج الحساسة أثناء المعالجة، في حين يركز الثاني على زيادة القدرة الحاسوبية وعرض نطاق الذاكرة لتشغيل تطبيقات الذكاء الاصطناعي التي تتطلب معالجة كميات كبيرة من المعلومات.
وقالت الشركة إن النظامين يمثلان تكوينين جديدين يعتمدان على رقائق موجودة من الجيل الثامن، وليس تصميمين جديدين للرقائق نفسها، إذ يشمل تطوير الأنظمة طريقة دمج الحوسبة والذاكرة والشبكات والتغليف وتقنيات الحماية.
صممت جوجل نظام TPU 8tx لتشغيل تطبيقات الاستدلال في بيئات الحوسبة السرية (Confidential Computing)، بهدف حماية البيانات الحساسة وأوزان النماذج أثناء الاستخدام، إلى جانب حمايتها عند التخزين أو النقل. ويستهدف النظام المؤسسات الحكومية والشركات في القطاعات الخاضعة لمتطلبات تنظيمية صارمة، التي تحتاج إلى تشغيل نماذج خاصة أو تطبيقات تعتمد على معلومات حساسة.
ويعتمد TPU 8tx على رقائق النظام TPU 8t نفسها، ويستخدم معالجات خوادم AMD EPYC من الجيل الخامس لتنسيق المهام وإعداد البيانات وإدارة الاتصال بوحدات تسريع الذكاء الاصطناعي.

items.t: Anthropic joins AI’s natural gas frenzy, buys $3.4B worth of turbines
items.d: Anthropic bought billions of dollars' worth of natural gas turbines in a deal that could give it buyer's remorse.
items.x:
Anthropic bought billions of dollars worth of natural gas turbines in a deal that could give it buyer's remorse.
AI’s power crunch has become so acute that Anthropic, a company that has generally avoided buying physical infrastructure, is spending $3.4 billion on natural gas turbines.
The AI company, which is planning to go public this year, is buying Caterpillar generators that equipment supplier OnePWR had originally ordered, according to a Financial Times report. The generators are capable of producing up to 1.7 gigawatts of electricity.
Historically, Anthropic has preferred to rent rather than buy. The company disclosed in its S-1 filing in May that it is paying SpaceX subsidiary xAI $1.25 billion per month through May 2029 to use xAI’s computing power.
“We expect to enter into additional similar services contracts,” Anthropic stated in the filing, meaning more deals to rent computing power.
But as demand for compute ramps up, the market for power has also grown increasingly uncertain, which may have forced its hand. The backlog for natural gas turbines stretches into the early 2030s, and queues to connect to the electrical grid can be just as long.
According to the report, OnePWR ordered the turbines a couple years ago, but couldn’t find financing to complete the purchase.

items.t: Medium’s new TK app brings AI assistance directly into the writing process
items.d: Medium's new writing app embraces AI-assisted writing, despite growing controversy over the technology's role in publishing.
items.x:
Medium's new writing app embraces AI-assisted writing, despite growing controversy over the technology's role in publishing.
Online publishing platform Medium on Monday launched a new app, called TK, which aims to bring AI technology deeper into the writing process. The idea behind TK is to make it easier to turn ideas into written words by incorporating an AI assistant into the editor itself, allowing users to ask for help by typing “@TK” followed by their request or prompt.
In publishing and journalism, the term “TK” serves as a placeholder used to mark where missing information can be added later. The “TK” stands for “to come,” but uses a “K” instead of “C” as there are few English words where the “tk” letter combination exists, making it stand out more easily in written text where it could be caught by proofreaders.
In Medium’s app, TK takes on a new role as it tries to help users fill in the blanks.
The company suggests the AI assistant could help answer questions that you might normally have to switch to another tab to quickly look up, like how many days are in a particular month.

items.t: Hold up — I had a great time talking to the RIAA guy
items.d: Today, I’m talking with Mitch Glazier, who is CEO and chairman of the RIAA. This conversation was a real full-circle moment for me: I was in college when Napster hit, and the RIAA became everyone’s villain for suing kids for downloading…
items.x:
Today, I’m talking with Mitch Glazier, who is CEO and chairman of the RIAA.
This conversation was a real full-circle moment for me: I was in college when Napster hit, and the RIAA became everyone’s villain for suing kids for downloading music. That was when I decided to go be a copyright lawyer, which set the rest of my career in motion — and Mitch was in the background as a young lawyer at the RIAA working on those cases. So part of me was very deeply, very genuinely surprised to discover just how much fun I had talking to Mitch.
That’s because here in 2026, Mitch, the RIAA, the record labels, the artists, and ordinary people are all pretty unhappy with the big AI companies in the same way, for training on everyone’s work without permission and flooding our feeds with slop.
Everyone is mad about it! And since the RIAA is both the group that lobbies for changes to the law and also the group that files lawsuits about things that affect record labels and distributors, Mitch is a pretty busy guy these days.

items.t: Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan: A Synthetic Dataset Capturing Japan's Demographics and Financial Context
items.x:
A compound AI approach to Japanese personas grounded in real-world distributions
In the financial sector, the utilization of real-world data faces significant constraints due to strict privacy regulations, compliance requirements, and the need for advanced domain expertise. In this context, the development of agentic AI in the financial domain requires synthetic data capable of avoiding the risks of using real data while reflecting demographics, household structures, and asset statuses to reproduce diverse, realistic financial scenarios.
To address these challenges, Elith and NVIDIA have released Nemotron-Personas-Finance-Japan, a financial domain extension of the open-source persona dataset "Nemotron-Personas-Japan." To our knowledge, it is the first open persona dataset at million-record scale that pairs Japan’s official statistics with household finance and financial literacy data. Built upon official government statistics, this dataset was developed using NeMo SDG-PGMs, a probabilistic graphical model framework for synthetic data generation (SDG), and NeMo Data Designer, an enterprise synthetic data generation system.

Automattic aims to compete with likes of Lovable with Spacefast
WordPress has been a crucial technology and content management system for websites like TechCrunch. Now, WordPress.com owner Automattic is responding to the changing state of the web by debuting a new service called Spacefast, which will allow users to deploy vibe-coded websites and apps.
Spacefast is designed to provide infrastructure for the vibe-coded apps, including databases, authentication, file uploads, emails, and analytics, to make them functional websites, apps, or services. The product competes with the likes of Lovable and Emergent, which offer both interface and rails for vibe-coded apps, but in a more open way.
Users can connect Spacefast with other agents and chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, Hermes, OpenClaw, Grokbot, Muse, Pi, Cursor, Opencode, and Amp. Alternatively, they can connect a Git repository to Spacefast to get started.
The product is headed by Batuhan Icoz, who worked on working on it during one of the company’s hackathon sprints earlier in the year.

As companies look to accelerate innovation with artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and advanced modeling, the primary challenge is connecting new technologies to reliable data, scientific expertise, and the practical realities of bringing products to market. For specialty chemicals manufacturer Lubrizol, digital transformation is all about giving researchers the tools to test ideas faster, make better-informed decisions, and develop more sustainable materials without compromising performance.
Girish Rao, vice president of information technology at Lubrizol, says the company is building a digital foundation that connects business processes, modern data platforms, and cloud infrastructure to support its research and development (R&D) teams. Their goal is to combine decades of accumulated technical data with the deep expertise of chemists and engineers who understand customer needs as well as the physical constraints of their work. Data scientists can help identify patterns, test new hypotheses, and model possibilities before researchers conduct physical experiments.

items.t: Your Experts Have Partners. There's HOPE for Keeping Them Together
items.x:
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have enabled state-of-the-art LLMs to be scaled to hundreds of billions of parameters, but they come with a fundamental and costly caveat: every expert MLP must occupy memory at inference time, even though the vast majority are idle for any given token. For example, Qwen3.5-122B has 256 experts in each of its 48 MoE layers, and 95% of its ~250 GB parameter memory footprint is taken up entirely by these expert MLPs alone. However, for any given token, only 8 experts in each layer are actually used.
Expert pruning is one of the most direct fixes to this memory bottleneck. That is, permanently delete the least useful experts. Pruning avoids the latency issues which make dynamic loading/off-loading of experts impractical; it does not require any training; and it composes with quantization. Given these attractive benefits and the simplicity of the idea, it's easy to see why expert pruning has become a go-to approach for shrinking MoEs. The difficulty lies in deciding which experts are safest to remove.
Existing pruning methods score each expert independently, assigning every expert a scalar importance score (based on a calibration dataset), and cutting out the least important experts (in each layer independently).

items.x:
The next chapter of competition in the automotive industry is beginning to unfold. Over the past few years, automakers have largely competed on electrification and price. But as electric vehicles become more widespread, relying solely on price cuts and cost controls is no longer a sustainable way to gain an edge. What consumers are increasingly willing to pay for is a better product experience and tangible value delivered by technology.
Patrick Cheng, CEO of SEEWAY.AI, said data and computing power will become increasingly important to the next decade of competition in China’s automotive industry. Companies that can make better use of data, build reliable computing foundations and turn AI technologies into large-scale applications will be better positioned to compete in the next phase of the industry.
Last Friday, SEEWAY.AI held its 2026 EVOLUTION Innovation Conference in Shanghai.

items.t: Goke Plans GK6950 Edge AI Chip Series for Embodied Robots, With 10 TOPS and VLA Support
items.d: Goke plans the GK6950 edge AI chip series for next year: 10 TOPS INT8, mixed precision for interactive models and FP16 spatial reconstruction.
items.x:
Goke Microelectronics is planning an edge AI chip series for human-machine interaction and embodied robots, called GK6950, which it says will launch next year. The plans were outlined on November 2 in Zhuhai by Ni Yayu, deputy head of the company's digital platform development department and its AI technical lead, at a supply-chain session held alongside the 2026 China Chip industry conference. The chip has not been released, and no samples, customers or availability dates were given.
According to Ni, the GK6950 series uses a new-generation on-device NPU architecture with 10 TOPS of dense INT8 compute. It supports mixed INT4, INT8, INT16 and FP16 precision, and is meant to handle traditional vision and audio perception, Transformer and large-model inference, and vision-language-action models on a single architecture.
The design is built around a specific robot workload: running an interactive large model and 3D spatial reconstruction at the same time. Goke says the same NPU operators support different precisions for each job. Language-model inference runs with 4-bit weights, FP16 activations and an INT8 key-value cache with paged management, to ease memory and bandwidth pressure from long contexts and concurrent streams.

items.t: TokenRhythm Opens Limited Beta for NeoHorse-1.5-Flash Preview, a 180B Agent-Focused Model
items.d: NeoHorse-1.5-Flash Preview, built on Qwen3.8-Flash with 6B active parameters, is in limited beta; company-run tests show gains on agent benchmarks.
items.x:
TokenRhythm, a Chinese AI infrastructure company that runs a multi-model routing platform, released NeoHorse-1.5-Flash Preview on November 5. The company describes it as an agent-native model aimed at task execution and software engineering. It is available only through a limited beta, for which users apply via the company's official WeChat account.
According to TokenRhythm, the model is trained on Qwen3.8-Flash and has 180 billion total parameters, with 6 billion active. In the company's own comparison against that base model, overall scores rose by 9.23 points on Agents' Last Exam and 5.92 points on Natural Language to Repository. The company says physical-science tasks improved by more than 20 points, with gains also in developer tooling and testing, web development, and security and cryptography. These are company-run evaluations; independent results have not been published.
The release is pitched as the second round of TokenRhythm's work on recursive self-improvement. After NeoHorse-1 shipped in September, the company says it put that model back into its model pool, collected execution feedback from real tasks, and used it to train the next model.

items.t: China Telecom Upgrades TeleAgent to V3.0, Giving Its Agent a Dedicated Cloud Computer
items.d: TeleAgent V3.0 runs agent tasks on a dedicated cloud PC shared by phone, desktop and web clients, adds nine connectors and enterprise-only skills.
items.x:
China Telecom has upgraded TeleAgent, its in-house general-purpose AI agent, to version 3.0. The central change is what the company calls an "agent plus cloud computer" mode: instead of running tasks on the user's own machine, the agent can work inside a cloud environment configured like a real PC. Chinese telecom outlet C114 dated the upgrade November 6, and China Telecom confirmed it to the Shanghai Securities News on November 9.
According to China Telecom, the desktop, mobile and web versions all control the same cloud "host." A task started on a phone during a commute can be picked up on an office computer, and the updated mobile app can view progress and send new instructions to both cloud and desktop tasks. The company says this lets workloads such as 3D modeling, document processing, code generation and video editing run in the cloud without using local memory or processor capacity.
TeleAgent's own web manual adds operating detail. Each user is assigned a dedicated Windows cloud computer; local files must be uploaded before the agent can use them, and outputs are stored in a cloud workspace. The machine shuts down when idle and restarts on demand, and scheduled tasks can wake it automatically.

items.t: Is Jensen Huang’s job on the line? Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld estimates it’s ‘about a 50-50’
items.d: Nvidia’s board is investigating Jensen Huang over his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld thinks it’s roughly a coin flip whether Huang stays on as CEO.
items.x:
Nvidia’s board is investigating Jensen Huang over his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld thinks it’s roughly a coin flip whether Huang stays on as CEO.
Nvidia’s board announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation after CEO Jensen Huang told staff he was unfaithful to his wife. But this isn’t a case of just another CEO having an extramarital affair. The romantic interest is Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. officials believe is a Chinese spy who was feeding information back to Beijing. In short, the stakes reach well beyond Nvidia, given how many tech and financial partners depend on its place at the center of the booming AI economy. “I’m responsible for an entire industry,” Huang recently told Bloomberg in a sit-down.
A spokesperson for the Chinese Embassy in Washington dismissed the allegations in late October as “groundless smears and slanders,” and no one has been charged. But U.S. intelligence officials reportedly briefed President Donald Trump about their concerns a year ago, and unnamed senior officials inside the Trump administration told the Times that they doubt Huang could have remained unaware all that time of Alice Huang’s intelligence-gathering role for China.

The country’s industry leaders are applying accelerated computing, AI and simulation to everything from semiconductor manufacturing to robotics and autonomous vehicles.
These efforts are helping bring physical AI from development into real-world production.
Samsung Advances Semiconductor Engineering With Accelerated Computing and AI Physics
Samsung Electronics is expanding its collaboration with NVIDIA to advance semiconductor innovation through accelerated computing and AI physics. The work spans materials research, process development and device engineering.
In technology computer-aided design, Samsung is working with NVIDIA cuISS and NVIDIA cuDSS to accelerate computations involving sparse linear systems. The collaboration also extends to GPU acceleration for process and optical simulations. In materials research, Samsung’s sMOL platform has run selected quantum chemical calculations up to 5x faster end to end with NVIDIA cuEST .

items.x:
As AI agents take on more work, they need capable open models and security that advances alongside them.
Hyundai Motor Group is exploring NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and the NVIDIA OpenShell runtime, while AIM Intelligence is integrating its Starfort platform with NVIDIA OpenShell to support secure AI agents for employee productivity and enterprise workflows .
A key component of the NVIDIA Open Agent Safety Platform, OpenShell provides a secure runtime with sandboxed execution and policy-based controls to safeguard sensitive data, manage access to enterprise tools and govern autonomous agent actions.
AIM Intelligence , a Korean AI security company, is integrating its Starfort agent control platform with NVIDIA OpenShell. The goal is to combine OpenShell’s runtime access controls with Starfort’s detection of malicious instructions and data leakage.

items.t: NVIDIA Dynamo Recipes Bring Korea’s Leading Open Models to Production
items.d: NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom, K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research, Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies. As models grow beyond the…
items.x:
NVIDIA is releasing Dynamo-optimized deployment recipes for Korea’s leading open models: A.X K2 from SK Telecom , K-EXAONE 2.0 from LG AI Research , Solar Open 2 from Upstage and Motif-3 from Motif Technologies .
As models grow beyond the capacity of a single GPU, they must be split across multiple GPUs, requiring careful coordination of request routing and communication to maintain performance.
NVIDIA Dynamo is an open source, distributed inference-serving framework built to deploy models in multi-node environments at data center scale. It handles this routing and communication to maximize inference performance.
Optimized for NVIDIA B200 GPUs, these recipes take the guesswork out of deployment, delivering up to 2x performance out of the box. They help developers bring Korea’s open models into production faster and turn them into broadly accessible AI for All services.

items.t: China Mobile Cloud and Zhipu Plan GLM Integration, Coding Products and Token Research
items.d: China Mobile Cloud and Zhipu plan GLM integration on MoMA, token-efficiency research and joint AI coding products; deployment details remain undisclosed.
items.x:
China Mobile Cloud and Zhipu have signed a cooperation agreement covering model services, AI coding products and industry applications. The agreement was signed on November 6 and reported by Chinese outlets on November 8; it is a partnership announcement rather than the launch of a finished joint service.
According to a Chinese-language report drawing on China Mobile Cloud's announcement, the companies plan to establish a joint development center focused on tokens. Their technical work will include adapting models to domestic computing hardware and optimizing models, with the stated aim of improving token-production efficiency. No measured efficiency improvement or implementation timetable was disclosed.
The agreement also calls for Zhipu's GLM model family to connect to China Mobile Cloud's MoMA model-service platform. This would bring the models into the operator's model-service offering, but the announcement does not establish that every GLM version is already available there. It does not specify supported versions, customer access arrangements or a service-level commitment.
Another strand is jointly developed AI coding products.

We’ve upgraded Claude Fable and Claude Mythos—models that are designed to tackle the most daunting technical challenges.
Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision. During prerelease testing they’ve helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours—among many other applications we’ll discuss below.
Claude Fable and Claude Mythos are the same underlying model. Fable has strong cybersecurity and biology safeguards to guard against misuse, which allows us to make it available to all users. Organizations pursuing beneficial applications in cybersecurity or biomedical research can apply for access to Mythos through our recently expanded Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs.
Testers have found that Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 communicate more clearly than past Fable and Mythos models.

items.t: Testing Claude on real-world electronics design
items.d: We asked Claude Fable 5.2 to design three electronic devices from short prompts: a speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub, and a handheld virtual pet. Diode Computers built working prototypes from its files.
items.x:
We asked Claude to design three electronic devices: a speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub, and a handheld virtual pet. The prototypes worked without any fixes to their circuitry.
A little over a year ago, we began testing how well Claude could design basic electronic circuits. We collaborated with Diode Computers,1 a company that designs and manufactures circuit boards, to train Claude on simple tasks—for example, on reading a chip’s datasheet and working out which parts a chip needs in order to run. The models we experimented with back then couldn’t reliably lay out a circuit board; they also struggled to design components that fit together. Now, Claude can both design and prototype electronic hardware from start to finish.
Engineering an electronic device requires working through many complex steps and practical constraints.

items.t: Which Claude model should you build with?
items.d: How to choose between Claude Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Haiku 5.5 by task, cost, and effort level.
items.x:
Which Claude model to pick, what they cost, and how to use them together.
The current Claude lineup has four generally available models: Claude Haiku 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2. Claude Mythos 5.2 is our most capable model for cybersecurity and life sciences research, available through our verification programs.
If you build on the Claude Platform or work in Claude Code, you may be wondering which model to use for your common tasks. This article will help answer that question and how to think about the trade-offs.
The quick answer is that you should start most work on Opus 5.5 at its default effort level, medium.
There's a reason it's the default model in Claude Code. It costs half as much per input and output token as Fable 5.2, and it's the model we recommend starting with for most coding and knowledge work.
Before you move models, try adjusting your effort level. It's a finer dial for both cost and capability. Past high, one more effort level can cost as much as a bigger model, so compare both on your own work. If you're past high, test the next model up at a lower effort instead.

items.t: Safely scaling multi-agent teams with Claude Fable 5.2
items.d: How a team of 1,000 agents running an early version of Claude Fable 5.2 reproduced a formal proof of Fermat's Last Theorem with general tools, a shared database, and layered safety controls.
items.x:
How a team of 1,000 agents running an early version of Claude Fable 5.2 reproduced a formal proof of Fermat's Last Theorem with general tools, a shared database, and layered safety controls.
Multi-agent teams can solve challenging, long-horizon problems. In September, we published the first end-to-end formalization of Fermat’s Last Theorem, written by dozens of agents running an internal research model roughly comparable to Claude Fable 5.1. That work relied on Prove2Me, a platform for formalizing mathematics, and direction from a researcher. In a new toy experiment, a team of 1,000 agents running an early version of Claude Fable 5.2 reproduced the proof without the scaffolding provided by Prove2Me or steering from a researcher. The team took 28.7 hours, used one-third as many output tokens, and wrote a proof one-seventh the length of the original.
Each agent worked in a sandbox with no internet access. A classifier checked every shell command and file edit before it ran, and an offline monitor reviewed each of the team’s actions. We gave the agents a list of 60 statements, a one-sentence sketch of the classical route, the definitions those statements use, and 47 proved lemmas from our earlier formalization, and assigned lead and helper roles.

Nvidia’s board of directors announced Sunday that it’s launching an independent investigation following reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a Chinese spy operation.
Nvidia also published a message that Huang sent to the company admitting that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. A memo circulating among U.S. policymakers earlier this year claimed that Alice Huang had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on Nvidia’s CEO.

“To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me,” he said.

items.t: الكونغرس الأمريكي يطلب إيضاحات من رئيس إنفيديا بشأن مزاعم تجسس صيني
items.d: طلبت ثلاث لجان في مجلس النواب الأمريكي إحاطة مغلقة من رئيس إنفيديا جنسن هوانغ على خلفية مزاعم تجسس صيني نقلتها تقارير صحفية، فيما تنفي الشركة مشاركة معلومات حساسة.
items.x:
طلب الكونغرس الأمريكي إحاطة مغلقة مع جنسن هوانغ رئيس إنفيديا بشأن مزاعم تجسس صيني أثارتها تقارير صحفية، وسط نفي الشركة مشاركة معلومات حساسة.
طلب رؤساء ثلاث لجان في مجلس النواب الأمريكي عقد إحاطة مغلقة مع الرئيس التنفيذي لشركة إنفيديا (Nvidia)، جنسن هوانغ، على خلفية تقارير صحفية تتناول صلات مزعومة لسيدة أعمال صينية بأجهزة الاستخبارات الصينية، ومخاوف بشأن حماية المعلومات الحساسة المتعلقة بتقنيات أشباه الموصلات والذكاء الاصطناعي.
وفي تطور لاحق، نقل موقع Axios عن السيناتور الديمقراطي كريس كونز عزمه النظر في المعلومات التي أثارتها التقارير. ولا تعني هذه التحركات إثبات وقوع تجسس أو تورط رئيس إنفيديا في أي مخالفة.
وجّه رؤساء لجان الشؤون الخارجية والاستخبارات واللجنة المختارة المعنية بالصين في مجلس النواب، برايان ماست وجون مولينار وريك كروفورد، خطابًا إلى هوانغ في 4 نوفمبر 2026 يطلبون فيه إحاطة مغلقة يوم 18 نوفمبر، مع الرد على الطلب بحلول 11 نوفمبر.
وتناول الخطاب المخاوف المثارة في تقارير إعلامية بشأن تواصل هوانغ مع أليس هوانغ، وهي سيدة أعمال مرتبطة بشركة ميجاسبيد (Megaspeed)، وإجراءات حماية المعلومات والتقنيات الأمريكية الحساسة. ويُعد الخطاب طلبًا للحصول على إيضاحات، وليس نتيجة تحقيق تثبت صحة المزاعم.
استندت المخاوف إلى تقارير صحفية أمريكية تحدثت عن احتمال وجود ارتباطات استخباراتية صينية لسيدة الأعمال المذكورة، وعن محاولات محتملة للحصول على معلومات مرتبطة بمعالجات الذكاء الاصطناعي.

items.t: After the midterms, things are looking rocky for Elon Musk and data centers
items.d: On Equity, we unpacked what the midterms mean for the tech industry.
items.x:
On Equity, we unpacked what the midterms mean for the tech industry.
Democrats’ historic victory in this week’s midterm elections could also have a dramatic effect on the tech industry.
In dozens of local ballot measures, voters rejected data centers. And even when they weren’t voting on the issue directly, they were electing politicians — like Texas’ new governor-elect Gina Hinojosa — who campaigned on the promise of restricting data centers.
On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O’Kane, and I discussed what the midterms mean for the tech industry. Sean kicked it off by noting that Elon Musk “seems to have basically nothing out of donating half a billion dollars” to Republicans, while his companies are now headquartered “in a state that has, remarkably, turned about as blue as it could possibly turn.”
And Kirsten said that while data centers probably weren’t the main cause of the “blue wave,” they’ve become an “an increasingly grassroots issue, in part because of how hyperscalers and companies have gone about” getting their projects approved.

items.t: OpenCSG Releases Agentic-27B for Tool Workflows, With Commercial Use Requiring Permission
items.d: OpenCSG's 27B agent model targets tool selection and failure recovery, with single-A800 test results. Its license requires permission for commercial use.
items.x:
OpenCSG has released Agentic-27B, a downloadable model designed for multi-step tool use and private enterprise deployments. Its Chinese technical introduction describes a focus on selecting Skills, constructing tool arguments, recovering from failures and checking whether an assigned task is actually complete.
The release is the second public version in the company's Agentic series. It replaces the earlier Qwen3-30B-A3B mixture-of-experts base with the dense Qwen3.8-27B model. OpenCSG says it used low-rank adaptation and direct preference optimization, or LoRA DPO, on execution records generated through its platform.
The preference-training dataset grew from roughly 3,000 examples to 5,857. OpenCSG says those samples include tool-use trajectories, low-scoring answers, failed calls and verification feedback, with records redacted, checked and screened before training. The model has about 27.36 billion parameters and BF16 weights.
All reported benchmark results come from OpenCSG. In its Agentic Eval, the company reports an average score of about 0.83, placing second among the models in that run.

items.t: AI broke the cybersecurity world. What’s next?
items.d: Today, I’m talking with Alex Stamos, chief security officer at Cognition and longtime cybersecurity expert, about what a mess cybersecurity is right now. This episode is part one of a special series looking at AI in real life. I’ve always…
items.x:
Today, I’m talking with Alex Stamos, chief security officer at Cognition and longtime cybersecurity expert, about what a mess cybersecurity is right now.
This episode is part one of a special series looking at AI in real life.
I’ve always enjoyed talking to Alex because he’s so direct, and you’re going to hear him say that the multibillion-dollar cybersecurity industry as we’ve known it is essentially overdue to the unrelenting, AI-boosted waves of hacks, breaches, and attacks — and this is only the beginning of how much AI is changing security.
Both private actors and also state actors, like Russia or North Korea, are breaking into systems all over thanks to AI helping them both detect and exploit vulnerabilities all at the same time. It’s got a real frontier feel to it, Alex notes, just like the ’90s, when the whole idea of an always-online world was brand-new.
That much disruption means a lot of places where bad guys can get in while everyone else is left scrambling.

items.t: From the front row to the hot seat — what the midterms mean for Big Tech
items.d: After spending two years getting cozy with the White House, Big Tech is suddenly trying to make friends with Democrats, and the open question is whether that image makeover can hold up against what states, local communities, and the…
items.x:
After spending two years getting cozy with the White House, Big Tech is suddenly trying to make friends with Democrats, and the open question is whether that image makeover can hold up against what states, local communities, and the markets are about to do.
Right before the midterm elections, OpenAI hired Jessica Schumer, daughter of Democratic Sen. Chuck Schumer. The company also said it would start calling its data centers “compute campuses.”
For the past two years, many of Silicon Valley’s biggest names have built closer ties with President Donald Trump and his administration. Several attended White House events, some companies scaled back diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) programs, and some executives donated millions to super PACs supporting his campaign and allied candidates. Administration policies also benefited the industry, including tax breaks, the pausing of some federal investigations, and looser AI regulation. Meanwhile, Meta faced lawsuits and billion-dollar fines and OpenAI faced suits alleging its technology harmed users.
Now, with the midterms shifting the balance of power in Washington, those same companies are working to rebuild ties with Democrats, who have pledged to tighten oversight of AI.

items.t: NearLink Alliance Publishes Embodied AI Connectivity Blue Book With 30-Plus Contributors
items.d: More than 30 contributors helped define NearLink connectivity requirements for robot internals, multi-device collaboration and device-edge-cloud coordination.
items.x:
The International SparkLink Alliance has published a blue book setting out short-range connectivity requirements for embodied AI, extending the NearLink ecosystem's focus into robot communications. The document went online on November 6, according to the alliance's announcement reported by IT Home .
More than 30 core members of the alliance's embodied-intelligence special interest group helped prepare the report. Contributors include China Mobile's research institute, Huawei, ZTE and TD Tech. The alliance says the work gathers practical technical requirements and proposes a full-stack technology and network architecture to guide joint development across the industry.
The blue book organizes those requirements around three scenarios: connections within a single robot, collaborative interactions among multiple devices, and coordinated scheduling across devices, edge systems and the cloud. That scope places the communication layer alongside the sensors, controllers and computing resources needed to operate embodied systems, rather than treating wireless links only as a connection to an external application.
Internal robot connectivity concerns links inside the machine itself.

items.t: Moore Threads Adds Day-Zero Kimi K3.1 Pro Support on MTT S5000 GPUs
items.d: Moore Threads says MTT S5000 and MUSA can load and serve Kimi K3.1 Pro with text and image inference, including sparse-attention and online weight-conversion support.
items.x:
Moore Threads says its MTT S5000 AI training and inference card and MUSA software stack have completed day-zero adaptation for Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro. The work connects model loading, service startup and basic text and image inference, according to the company's announcement reported by IT Home on November 6.
The announcement describes functional deployment rather than a published performance comparison. Moore Threads said it migrated the model's key inference paths and enabled stable execution on MTT S5000, but the report did not provide throughput, latency, power consumption or the number of cards used. Its day-zero description is the company's characterization; Moonshot released the full model weights on November 4.
At the framework level, the team used SGLang-MUSA to build on the upstream model implementation. The migration also involved the MATE operator library, Triton-MUSA, TileLang-MUSA and the MTCC compiler. MUSA covers framework execution, operator compilation, device runtime and communication across multiple cards, allowing developers to reuse existing interfaces while adapting new computation paths.
Much of the model-specific work concerned attention and memory handling.

items.t: Crusoe sells troubled Wyoming data center project to Google
items.d: The deal highlights the challenges of developing massive AI data centers.
items.x:
The deal highlights the challenges of developing massive AI data centers.
Crusoe, an eight-year-old, Denver-based data center developer recently valued at $30.9 billion, confirmed Friday it has sold an unfinished data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google.
Google, which Crusoe had tried and failed to land as a customer for the project, is taking over the development after reportedly raising concerns about its cost and construction timeline under Crusoe’s management.
Crusoe initially announced the project last year with Blackstone-backed infrastructure company Tallgrass, planning to eventually scale it to 10 gigawatts of power capacity.
Google did not disclose how much it paid Crusoe for the unfinished project, bu it announced plans to invest $17 billion to develop the data center campus.
The deal highlights how difficult it can be for independent data center developers to deliver massive projects on time and within budget, given the challenges of securing equipment and power. Growing opposition from local communities can further complicate development.
Despite taking over the Wyoming facility, Google hasn’t walked away from working with Crusoe entirely.

Security researchers found hundreds of servers hosting the penetration testing tool Artex exposed to the internet, allowing anyone access to the hacking tool.
Security researchers have discovered hundreds of copies of a Chinese-made AI hacking tool publicly exposed to the internet for anyone to access, potentially allowing outsiders to launch cyberattacks against unsuspecting targets.
The hacking software, called Artex, is an open-source autonomous penetration testing tool, meaning software that automatically probes computer systems for weaknesses, and it’s been linked to several cyberattacks since its public release in July. As open-source software, it’s free for anyone to download and run on their own servers, making it a popular tool for those who cannot access Anthropic or OpenAI’s most advanced cybersecurity AI models for discovering security vulnerabilities.

AI usage keeps climbing, but spending has stalled. Price cuts and smarter cost controls among the biggest spenders could challenge investor assumptions about AI hypergrowth.
Companies are using more AI than ever, but they’re not spending more on it.
A new report from Ramp shows AI spending flatlined over late summer even as token volumes rose, a sign that price competition and savvier customers may be capping revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. According to Ramp’s data, token spend only grew 1.5% across August and September. To compare, in July, it grew 42% from the previous month.
As Anthropic gears up for its IPO, the data suggests investors might be wrong to assume AI companies will keep growing at breakneck speed.
“Almost the entire spend on AI is from venture-backed, high-growth tech companies,” Ramp’s lead economist Ara Kharazian told TechCrunch.

items.t: ToyBlocks: A controlled world for robot learning and evaluation
items.x:
Robots are learning to fold laundry, sort parts, and handle unfamiliar objects. But those demonstrations are often rather narrow and don't explain what a robot has learned or why it fails.
To study a complex system, scientists often begin with a small, controlled environment, such as a petri dish or terrarium, where they can vary conditions and observe the effects. Robotics needs environments that make this kind of investigation possible—researchers should be able to change the training data or model design, repeat a test, and trace the cause of a failure.
Today we're introducing a framework for creating these environments; we call them FoundationWorlds. Each pairs a controlled, simulated world targeted at studying robotics in a specific environment with tools for automatically generating tasks and training demonstrations, as well as metrics for measuring a robot's behavior over time. Together, they provide a setting for studying questions such as how models improve as more training data becomes available, and how to best combine high-level reasoning with precise physical control.
Our first foundation world is ToyBlocks: an open simulation framework built around a robot arm and blocks on a tabletop.

I’m not the sort of person who typically pays for a house cleaner. I’m too frugal, and I kind of enjoy putting on a podcast and going to town on my tub with a Magic Eraser. But when I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning service in San Francisco, I immediately signed up for the waitlist. I wanted my apartment to feel like The Jetsons , even if just for an hour.
I was also motivated by journalistic interest. In order to ensure an authentic experience, I didn’t tell Tau Robotics, the startup behind the X post, that I was a journalist—though I did use my real name, so it’s possible someone looked me up. Tau’s long-term goal is to make autonomous cleaning robots a reality, but they’re not quite there yet: For now, the robots are piloted remotely by humans, who watch what’s going on via cameras mounted in the robots’ heads and wrists. As the robots clean, they collect data that Tau will use to train up their more independent descendants. Every counter successfully wiped and T-shirt successfully folded will help the models that power the robots learn to do better on the next go-round.
Because this data is so valuable to Tau, the company charges less for cleaning than one might expect for such a cutting-edge product.

But Qwen’s rise was anything but smooth: internal skepticism, fierce competition and senior departures shaped the model long before it became a global name.
Qwen’s path to Apple did not begin as the story of an inevitable champion.
Alibaba introduced Tongyi Qianwen in April 2023, months after ChatGPT jolted China’s technology industry into a race to build large language models. It soon began releasing model weights publicly, gradually making open source central to Qwen’s strategy.
Even inside Alibaba, Qwen was not the automatic choice . Some teams kept using Meta’s Llama well into 2024, while Fliggy and Alibaba.com later experimented with DeepSeek’s R1. The model had to win over its own company before it could win over the wider market.
Open source became part of the answer.

Youdao frames the product around a common frustration: students can read a worked solution and still not understand why an auxiliary line goes where it does in a geometry problem, or how to handle a function question once the conditions change. The company says the agent is meant to move students from understanding an answer to being able to solve similar problems on their own.
The tutoring flow has three parts. First, the agent hints at a direction before walking through the key derivations and calculations one step at a time, and it ends by naming the method used and the core concept the question tests. Second, students can stop at any step and ask follow-up questions, so the explanation adjusts to where they are stuck instead of running through a fixed script.
Third, the agent draws.

items.t: Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science
items.d: OpenAI introduces BioBasicsBench, a 100-task benchmark measuring how well AI agents interpret raw experimental data and handle everyday wet-lab science.
items.x:
OpenAI introduces BioBasicsBench, a 100-task benchmark measuring how well AI agents interpret raw experimental data and handle everyday wet-lab science.
Introducing BioBasicsBench, a benchmark measuring how well AI agents interpret raw experimental data across 100 routine wet-lab tasks.
Our mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. As part of that mission, we want to help scientists accelerate biological research—from understanding disease to developing new treatments. For AI agents to contribute, they need to reliably interpret the experimental evidence scientists work with every day in wet labs, where they run experiments with biological samples. Everyday wet-lab work involves failed experiments, ambiguous images and conflicting observations. Existing benchmarks are built around charts and images selected for scientific papers may miss this ambiguity and the troubleshooting it requires. That’s why we’re introducing BioBasicsBench, a new benchmark developed with Ligo, a biotech company focused on enzyme design, to measure how well agents handle routine wet-lab analysis.
The benchmark’s 100 tasks test whether agents can interpret raw experimental data, identify errors, and recognize when the evidence cannot support a conclusion.
